Lututow Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Lututów, Poland

Demolished. Lututów, founded in 1406, saw individual Jewish families settle in the 18th century; a conditional 1844 royal steward's agreement accelerated settlement, and a kehilla formed by mid-century. Jews became the majority population from the late 19th into the early 20th century, still 68.8% (1,466 total) by 1921. A 1940 ghetto held approximately 1,200; its August 1942 liquidation split residents between the Łódź Ghetto and Chełmno. This cemetery, established sometime in the mid-19th century on a hill called 'Młynek,' was destroyed with local involvement during WWII; a gravel and sand mine replaced it, with skulls and bones scattered in nearby woods and roadsides. The site is now illegally used as a refuse dump.
